standard_prerequisites.name: The negative vanishing property of derived functors under the canonical truncation
For a K-injective resolution the functor applied to the complex agrees with the derived limit of its truncations, and the cohomology of a derived limit is computed by the Rlim short exact sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Expresses H^i(RF(E)) via the inverse system of the truncated values.

standard_prerequisites.name: The truncation triangles produce maps between the truncated systems whose cohomology maps are isomorphisms past the cohomological dimension bound, giving the ML condition and eventual constancy
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows the R^1lim term vanishes and the limit term stabilizes to the value at a finite truncation.

core_obligations: Statement (1) is Derived Categories, Lemma negative-vanishing (proof lines 395-397).

Proof of (2): write E_n = tau_{>= -n}E; since E = Rlim E_n by Lemma nice-K-injective, RF(E) = Rlim RF(E_n) in D(Ab) by Injectives, Lemma RF-commutes-with-Rlim, giving for each i the short exact sequence with R^1lim H^{i-1}(RF(E_n)) on the left and lim H^i(RF(E_n)) on the right (More on Algebra, Remark compare-derived-limit); the goal is to show the left term is zero and the right term equals H^i(RF(E_{-b+N-1})) for i >= b (proof lines 400-412).

For every n the truncation triangle H^{-n}(E)[n] to E_n to E_{n-1} to H^{-n}(E)[n+1] (Derived Categories, Remark truncation-distinguished-triangle) gives, since H^{-n}(E) is quasi-coherent and R^pF vanishes for p >= N, that H^i(RF(E_n)) to H^i(RF(E_{n-1})) is an isomorphism for n >= N - i; hence the systems satisfy the ML condition and are constant from n = N - i - 1 on, so the R^1lim term is zero and the limit term is as claimed, proving (2) (proof lines 414-437).

Proof of (3): if H^i(E) = 0 outside [a, b], then tau_{<= a-1}E = 0 and (1) gives H^i(RF(E)) = 0 for i <= a - 1, while tau_{>= b+1}E = 0 and (2) gives H^i(RF(E)) = 0 for i >= b + N; altogether H^i(RF(E)) = 0 outside [a, b + N - 1] (proof lines 439-447).
proof_roadmap: Express H^i(RF(E)) through the Rlim sequence over truncations (proof lines 400-412).
Prove ML and eventual constancy from the truncation triangles and the dimension bound (proof lines 414-437).
Combine the one-sided bounds into the amplitude statement (3) (proof lines 439-447).
